description: Cross-cutting code idioms ('mechanics') tagged on lessons so the user can drill the same pattern across every place it appears. Each lesson's `mechanics` field references entries by id here.

mechanics.label: Nested-loop build
mechanics.blurb: Two nested loops that push each combination into an output array. The shape behind Cartesian products, deck construction, matrix initialization, and pair enumeration.

mechanics.label: Array transform chain
mechanics.blurb: Compose map / filter / reduce / sort / slice into a single expression. Reads top-to-bottom as a pipeline; great when intermediate names would just be noise.

mechanics.label: Two-pointer convergence
mechanics.blurb: Left and right indices walk toward each other based on a comparison. Sorted-array problems collapse from O(n^2) to O(n).

mechanics.label: Sliding window (expand / shrink)
mechanics.blurb: Right pointer expands the window; left pointer shrinks it whenever an invariant breaks. Maintains a running aggregate so each element is touched O(1) amortized.

mechanics.label: Fast & slow pointers
mechanics.blurb: Two pointers move at different speeds. Floyd's tortoise-and-hare for cycle detection; mid-of-list trick; nth-from-end with a gap.

mechanics.label: Hash complement lookup
mechanics.blurb: Walk the array once; for each element ask 'have I seen its complement?' Check BEFORE inserting so you can't match an element with itself.

mechanics.label: Frequency map
mechanics.blurb: Count occurrences of each key in a single pass. The `(get(k) ?? 0) + 1` idiom handles the first-time-seen case without a branch.

mechanics.label: Set for dedup / membership
mechanics.blurb: `new Set(arr)` removes duplicates in one shot; `Set` membership is O(1). Use over `arr.includes()` whenever the same array is queried repeatedly.

mechanics.label: Array-as-stack
mechanics.blurb: Use a plain array as a LIFO stack: push to add, pop to remove, `at(-1)` to peek. The shape behind bracket matching, DFS, undo history, monotonic stacks.

mechanics.label: Array-as-queue
mechanics.blurb: Push to enqueue, shift to dequeue. `shift` is O(n) on huge arrays — for production code use a head index — but for interview-scale n it's fine.

mechanics.label: BFS with level snapshot
mechanics.blurb: Snapshot `queue.length` BEFORE the inner loop so children pushed mid-loop are processed in the NEXT outer iteration. Lets you process one level at a time.

mechanics.label: Grid flood-fill DFS
mechanics.blurb: Recursive DFS into a grid with bounds + visited guard at the TOP. Mutating the grid in-place doubles as 'visited' and skips an auxiliary set.

mechanics.label: 4-directional neighbor walk
mechanics.blurb: The four cardinal deltas as a single array, iterated with destructuring. Bounds-check BEFORE indexing — otherwise edges crash.

mechanics.label: Heap index math + sift
mechanics.blurb: 0-indexed array heap: parent=(i-1)>>1, left=2i+1, right=2i+2. Sift up after push (compare with parent); sift down after pop-root (swap with smaller child).

mechanics.label: Linked-list prev / curr walk
mechanics.blurb: Cache `curr.next` BEFORE rewiring or you lose the rest of the list. The prev/curr/next triple is the shape behind reverse, remove-nth, reorder.

mechanics.label: Tree recursion (left + right)
mechanics.blurb: Null root → base case; recurse on left + right; combine the two results. The shape behind depth, invert, validate-BST, max-path-sum.

mechanics.label: Backtracking: choose / explore / un-choose
mechanics.blurb: Push a choice → recurse with the next decision → pop the choice. The pop is the backtrack — without it, sibling branches inherit state from this one.

mechanics.label: Constructor delegates to reset()
mechanics.blurb: Put initialization in a `reset()` method and have the constructor call it. Now the caller can rebuild state without re-instantiating — useful for decks, boards, game state.

mechanics.label: Closure capturing private state
mechanics.blurb: Return a function that closes over locals. The state is unreachable from outside — pure encapsulation without a class. The shape behind counters, memoize, throttle, debounce.

mechanics.label: DP with rolling variables
mechanics.blurb: When DP only needs the last 1-2 values, drop the array and keep two scalars. Space goes from O(n) to O(1) without touching the recurrence.

mechanics.label: DP bottom-up tabulation
mechanics.blurb: Allocate a dp array sized by the input; fill bottom-up so each entry's dependencies are already computed. Iterative, no recursion stack risk.

mechanics.label: DP top-down memoization
mechanics.blurb: Plain recursion + a `Map` cache keyed by the subproblem. Check cache first, recurse if missing, store before returning. Great when the state space is sparse.

mechanics.label: Async IIFE
mechanics.blurb: Wrap top-level await in `(async () => { ... })()` so you can use await outside an async function. The runner awaits the returned promise.

mechanics.label: Promise chain / await
mechanics.blurb: Two equivalent shapes: `.then(...).then(...)` chains promises in order; `await` lets the same flow read like synchronous code.

mechanics.label: Destructured arguments
mechanics.blurb: Destructure the parameter at the function boundary so callers pass an options object and the body uses bare names. Defaults can sit right in the pattern.

mechanics.label: Spread for merge / copy
mechanics.blurb: `{ ...a, ...b }` shallow-merges objects (later wins); `[...a, ...b]` concatenates arrays. Used for immutable state updates, function arg forwarding, and shallow cloning.
mechanics.snippet:
const merged = { ...defaults, ...overrides };
const combined = [...first, ...second];

mechanics.label: XOR accumulator
mechanics.blurb: XOR is its own inverse and commutes, so XORing every element cancels duplicates and leaves the unique one. Identity is 0.

mechanics.label: Clear lowest set bit (n & (n-1))
mechanics.blurb: `n & (n - 1)` removes the lowest 1-bit of n. Loop until n is 0 to count set bits in O(popcount) instead of O(32).

mechanics.label: Binary search on a half-open interval
mechanics.blurb: Closed interval [l, r] with `while (l <= r)`, midpoint `m = (l + r) >> 1`, then narrow to `m+1` or `m-1`. The same skeleton drives sorted-array search AND predicate search on an answer space (Koko, ship-capacity, etc.).

mechanics.label: Dummy-head sentinel (linked list)
mechanics.blurb: Create a fake node before the real list, build off `dummy.next`, return `dummy.next` at the end. Removes the special case for an empty result OR for inserting before the original head — the rest of the code stops branching on `head === null`.

mechanics.label: Greedy single-pass scan
mechanics.blurb: Walk the array once, maintaining one or two running aggregates (best, current, total) and updating them with a local decision per element. Reset state when a prefix is provably non-useful (Kadane's, gas-station tank).

mechanics.label: Graph DFS over adjacency list
mechanics.blurb: Recursive (or stack-based) DFS over a `node → neighbors[]` adjacency map, with a `visited` set to break cycles. Distinct from grid DFS — neighbors come from a map, not from coordinate deltas.

mechanics.label: Sort then sweep
mechanics.blurb: Sort the input by a key, then walk it once with a small piece of running state (last merged interval, open-event count). The sort surfaces the relevant ordering so the scan can decide locally.

mechanics.label: Union-Find (Disjoint Set)
mechanics.blurb: `parent[i]` points each node at its representative; `find` walks up with path compression; `union` links two roots. O(α(n)) per op — effectively constant. Counts components, detects cycles in undirected graphs.

mechanics.label: Ring buffer with modular index
mechanics.blurb: Fixed-size array with a moving head/tail index that wraps via `% capacity`. Writes overwrite the oldest entry without reallocation. Used in circular buffers, rate limiters, and last-N caches.

mechanics.label: Map-keyed state container
mechanics.blurb: Use a Map (or plain object) keyed by event/category/id to hold per-key state — usually an array of listeners, a line-item record, or a counter. The `(get(k) ?? init)` set-on-first-touch idiom keeps the call sites branch-free.

mechanics.label: In-place matrix transpose / swap
mechanics.blurb: Swap `matrix[i][j]` with `matrix[j][i]` for `j > i` to transpose in place — then reverse each row to rotate 90° clockwise. Two simple passes replace allocating a new grid.

mechanics.label: Boundary-shrinking traversal (4 walls)
mechanics.blurb: Maintain top/bottom/left/right bounds; each pass walks one wall and contracts that bound inward. The shape behind spiral matrix and any 'peel the onion' grid walk.
